body: Transformers dispense with recurrence and convolutions and rely entirely on attention mechanisms [1]. Residual connections made it possible to train networks that are much deeper than earlier architectures [2]. Batch normalization reduces internal covariate shift and allows much higher learning rates [3]. Retrieval-augmented generation combines a parametric seq2seq model with a dense vector index of Wikipedia [4].
references: [1] Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., Uszkoreit, J., Jones, L., Gomez, A. N., Kaiser, Ł., & Polosukhin, I. (2017). Attention is all you need. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 30.
[2] He, K., Zhang, X., Ren, S., & Sun, J. (2016). Deep residual learning for image recognition. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 770–778).
[3] Kingma, D. P., & Ba, J. (2015). Adam: A method for stochastic optimization. In International Conference on Learning Representations.
[4] Kowalski, A., Dubois, M., & Sato, K. (2023). Self-verifying language agents for automated literature review. Nature Machine Intelligence, 5, 802–811.

quote: We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.
explanation: Replace the nonexistent reference [4] with Lewis et al. (2020), the paper that introduced RAG; its abstract states the claim almost verbatim. This is also the original source rather than a later application.

paper.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
paper.apa: Ioffe, S., & Szegedy, C. (2015). Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift. arXiv. http://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03167v3

quote: We refer to this phenomenon as internal covariate shift, and address the problem by normalizing layer inputs.
explanation: The Adam paper (Kingma & Ba) is an optimizer paper and says nothing about batch normalization, internal covariate shift, or higher learning rates. The correct citation is the original Batch Normalization paper by Ioffe & Szegedy, which introduces the method and the term "internal covariate shift"; it also states that "Batch Normalization allows us to use much higher learning rates and be less careful about initialization."
